Setup a monthly survival budget.

First priority, gun and some ammo.

Shotgun and buckshot (not birdshot or slugs unless you are physically large and strong and know how to handle a gun), find a local range, go and fire off rounds until you are comfortable with the gun. Then keep about 100 rounds with the gun.

Second, provisions.

Distilled water in plastic bottles will last pretty much forever if sealed properly. I prefer the 5 gallon bottles since they take up less space per gallon of water. Also, at least one life straw per person in the house.

Survival food. Keep at least two weeks per person. You can buy prepacked meals online and I believe costco has them also.

Meds.

Extra meds... you need extras. Don't fool yourself and think "I wont need my anti-depressants in the apocalypse." The first few days/weeks of an emergency situation are the most critical and you don't want to be dealing with withdrawal or having to worry about your inhalers running out if you have asthma or something.

First aid kit. Get a good one. Well stocked... burn gel, antiseptic cream, wraps and band-aids are the minimum.

Tools. If you don't have a good set of hand tools go get some. Axe, hammer, knife, saw. Don't get the cheap stuff.

Lastly... more ammo and more time at the range. Get good with that weapon.
